name: Goedel-Prover
org: Princeton Language and Intelligence (Princeton University), with Tsinghua University, Amazon, Meta FAIR and Numina
one_liner: A Lean 4 prover trained in rounds: each prover writes proofs, Lean checks them, and verified proofs train the next one.

loop.proposes: Lean 4 proofs for 1.64 million formalized statements
loop.judged_by: The Lean compiler, which checks each candidate proof
loop.steers: Verified proofs join the training set and the next, stronger prover is trained on them (expert iteration)

headline_result: Goedel-Prover-SFT reaches 57.6% Pass@32 on miniF2F, 7.6 points above DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL; the paper's abstract reports over 60% Pass@32 after RL including DPO, 7 PutnamBench problems at Pass@512, and proofs for 29.7K Lean Workbook problems versus 15.7K for prior provers.
caveat: Its best-result claims are dated April 2025 and use Pass@32 or Pass@512, so budgets differ from some rivals. The paper text says 8 iterations while a table lists Iter-9. The abstract does not describe the compiler signal beyond verification.
beyond_harness_note: Lean-verified proofs become the training data for the next generator, so feedback changes the model, and the proofs are checkable without it.

sources.title: Goedel-Prover: A Frontier Model for Open-Source Automated Theorem Proving

verification.notes: Read the abstract page and the paper's expert-iteration text via fetch. Added as one of the two extra provers; it has no inference-time search, so it passes the filter through its training loop. Affiliations as the fetch reported them.
